resume had zero nav chrome (own render()) - added one

at the top, two links, scrolls away with the page like everything else. blog/page.js rail() appended a plain {label:Resume,url:/resume/} entry after the section groups (Sidebar.nav() already treats a pages-less entry as a link) - verified present on both the front AND a post page, not just the magazine front's own About block.

assign.now: fix 3 done - sticky Depth/Motion bar, cause found and fixed

log.msg: CAUSE (measured with Playwright, not guessed): .resume-depth was width:fit-content + margin-inline:auto - a narrow centred pill. Sticky top:0 pins it correctly (perspective on the .depth-scene ancestor does NOT break sticky here, confirmed: computed transform none, position sticky held). Every heading passing y=0 during scroll passed UNDER the pill's narrow strip only - so part of a heading (outside the pill) stayed fully legible while the part inside it got sliced mid-glyph: an asymmetric cut, which read as broken. Fix: width:100% (matching the card column) + border-block-end instead of all-round border/radius - the bar now occludes a heading UNIFORMLY (a clean curtain, standard sticky-header behaviour) instead of biting a jagged chunk out of the middle of one word.

CUT, stated honestly: a control that must stay reachable while scrolling a long single-flow page will always have SOME heading transit behind it for an instant - that is true of every sticky header on the web and is not fixable without either abandoning sticky (breaks the strength the critique itself called out - drag the slider above at Selected Work) or moving the bar outside the resume-card's own column into the page's grey gutter, which needs the max-width constraint moved down a level (bigger than S, and touches the depth-scene's own container - the scroll machinery trap). Measured at a normal reading scroll (heading centred in viewport): 183px of clear air between bar and heading, zero overlap - the bug only bites in the ~35px transit band right at the top of the viewport, now cleanly occluded rather than jaggedly sliced.

assign.now: fix 4 done - ext/layout .layout-bar rest opacity 0 to 0.4

log.msg: one line: .layout > .layout-bar dropped its opacity:0 override, falling through to the bare .layout-bar rule's opacity:0.4 - same quiet-but-present convention nav/links and nav/rail's own toolbars already use at rest, per the critique's #15 (pick one convention sitewide). (hover:none) already forced opacity:1 and is untouched. Verified live on /web/layout/flex/ - bar visible, dimmed, at rest.

log.msg: zero console/page errors on: /resume/ (400, 1600, 1920, dark), /blog/, /blog/framework/how-this-blog-works/, /blog/systems/panel-playground/, /web/, /web/layout/grid/, /web/layout/flow/, /web/layout/flex/. Cross-links click both ways: resume corner links to / and /blog/; blog rail's Resume entry present on the front AND on a post page (was front-only before, via the About block, which still also has it).
